 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HASMUKH D. SUTHAR  Date : 05/03/2026  JUDGMENT
Though served, respondent No.2 has chosen not to appear before this Court.
ADMIT.
Learned advocate Mr. Nishit Bhalodi waives service of notice of Admission for and on behalf of respondent Nos.3, 4 and 5.

[1.0] Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned common judgment and award dated 22.12.2023 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.-III), Gandhinagar (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for short) in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.279/2015, the appellant Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Vastirambhai Dhokaji Oad on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163568636/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 - original opponent No.3 has preferred the present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short).

C/FA/3841/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
 
[2.0] The brief facts of the present case are that, 14.06.2015 in between 8 to 9 P.M., Kaushikbhai Dahyabhai Shah (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") and Sureshbhai Dahyabhai Shah were going on Motorcycle bearing No.GJ-1-NJ-9751, which was being driven by Kaushikbhai and Sureshbhai was pillion rider on the said motorcycle and when they reached at the place of accident, driving the motorcycle with slow speed on the correct side of road, driver of Dumper Truck bearing No.GJ-1-CV-7455 came driving his Dumper in rash and negligent manner endangering human life without following traffic rules and coming on wrong side of the road dashed with motorcycle No.GJ-1-NJ-9751 and thus, the accident took place causing death of deceased as well as the pillion rider on the motorcycle.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the original claimants - legal heirs of the deceased to get compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the opponents.
After appreciating the evidence produced on record, the learned Tribunal holding the driver of Dumper to be solely negligent awarded compensation of Rs.25,71,468/- along with cost and interest @ 8%
p.a . [3.0] The appeal is filed challenging exorbitant compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal and no further issue qua liability is raised.

[4.0] Learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company has submitted that the learned Tribunal has misread the salary slip (Exh.35) of the deceased and further erred in adopting actual salary Rs.29,244/- per month.

He has further argued that the learned Tribunal committed an error in adopting multiplier of 9 and in awarding 15% prospective rise in salary of the deceased though the deceased, at the time of accident, was aged 58 years and would have NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3841/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined retired on superannuation after two years.
Hence, he has prayed to allow the appeal as prayed for.
[5.0] Learned counsel for the original claimants has opposed the present appeal and submitted that,
the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation which does not call for any interference by this Court.
Therefore, requested to dismiss the appeal.

sentences.text: [6.0] Having considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, it appears that the appeal is filed only on the aspect of quantum and liability is not challenged.
Hence, this appeal is required to be decided on the aspect of quantum only.
Alleged incident is not in dispute.
Involvement of the vehicle is also not in dispute.

In order to prove the claim, the original claimant No.1 has filed an Affidavit at Exh.25, FIR at Exh.26, Panchnama of scene of incident at Exh.27,
Inquest Panchanama at Exh.36 and PM report at Exh.29.

After appreciating the evidence produced on record, the Tribunal held the offending vehicle Dumper solely negligent relying on the decisions of the Bimla Devi Vs. HRTC reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 and Parmeshwari Devi Vs. Amir Chand,
reported in 2011 (11) SCC 635.

entities.text: Bimla Devi Vs. HRTC reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Parmeshwari Devi Vs. Amir Chand,
reported in 2011 (11) SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, so far as negligence part is concerned, this Court is of considered view that no error has been committed by the learned Tribunal and does not call for any interference.

[7.0] Further, perusing the evidence produced on record, it appears that at the time of accident,
deceased was aged 56 years and was earning Rs.35,000/- per month by serving as driver in the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation, Gandhinagar (hereinafter referred to as "GSRTC").

entities.text: Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation, Gandhinagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
In support of their case, original claimants have produced salary slip of deceased for the month of May-2015 at Exh.35, which has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3841/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
05/03/2026 undefined been issued by the GSRTC, in which net salary of the deceased is mentioned as Rs.29,244/-.
Learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company has disputed the document (Exh.35) on the ground that no any witness is examined to substantiate the said document i.e. salary slip (Exh.35).

Learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company has submitted that since the deceased at the time of accident was aged 58 years and was to retire on superannuation at the age of 60 years i.e. after two years of the accident, the learned Tribunal ought not to have awarded 15%
prospective rise in salary.

At this stage, it is profitable to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of R. Valli & Ors v. Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd. reported in (2022) 5 SCC 107 wherein it has been held that actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax and multiplier strictly as per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (Supra) approved by Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra).

entities.text: R. Valli & Ors v. Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd. reported in (2022) 5 SCC 107
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [7.1] Further, it is needless to say that the GSRTC is a statutory body and the document (Exh.35) is issued by the GSRTC which is enough for guess work and therefore, the learned Tribunal has safely presumed the income of the deceased at Rs.29,244/- per month.

The claimant have also produced salary slips of deceased for the months of December- 2014; January-2015 and May-2015 respectively at Exhs.33, 34 and 35 and considering the said salary slips, the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.29,244/- per month.

Further, as the deceased was aged 58 years and in permanent government job, in view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017)
16 SCC 680, the learned Tribunal has rightly considered 15% addition towards future prospective income of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3841/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined the deceased and therefore, the future monthly income of the deceased at Rs.33,631/- [Rs.29,244 +
Rs.4387(15% of Rs.29,244)] is rightly assessed, which does not call for any interference.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017)
16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
[7.2] The learned Tribunal relying on the post-mortem report (Exh.29) of the deceased has come to the conclusion that the deceased at the time of accident was aged 58 years and therefore, in view of Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Vastirambhai Dhokaji Oad on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163568636/
3 the decision of Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. [2009 (6) SCC 121], as the deceased was having three dependents, the learned Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of '9' as the deceased fell in the age group of 56 to 60 years and rightly deducted 1/3rd amount towards personal expenses of the deceased which comes to Rs.11,210/- and remaining amount i.e. Rs.22,421/- is the amount towards monthly loss of family dependency and therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs.24,21,468/- (Rs.22,421 x 12 x 9) towards future loss of dependency, which does not call for any interference.

sentences.text:
So far as compensation awarded under other heads are concerned, in the considered opinion of this Court, the learned Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation under other heads and therefore, the original claimants are rightly awarded the compensation as under:
 Heads Awarded by the Tribuna  Future loss of dependency Rs.24,21,468/-
 Loss of Estate 15,000/-
 Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Loss of consortium Rs.1,20,000/-

Total compensation Rs.25,71,468/-
 
 C/FA/3841/2024 JUDGMENT DAT
[8.0] Hence, present appeal being devoid of any merit stands dismissed.

The appellant herein - insurance company is directed to deposit compensation of Rs.25,71,468/- along with interest as awarded by the Tribunal, before the Tribunal within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment and thereafter, the learned Tribunal to disburse the entire amount of compensation alongwith accrued interest thereon, if any, to the original claimants, by account payee cheque /
NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure and strictly in accordance with the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal.
[9.0] While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid.
] Record
and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
